programme: EBF1, AKNA, ZFPM1 and HHEX form a hematolymphoid transcription-factor kit that builds and activates local lymphoid tissue rather than any single cell type: EBF1 is the master driver of B-lymphocyte lineage commitment (its targets PAX5, CD19, CD79A, VPREB1, IGLL1, BCR, PRDM1, FOXO1 are the canonical B-cell differentiation program); AKNA reaches only CD40 and CD40LG, the receptor-ligand pair that licenses T-cell-dependent B-cell activation and germinal-center formation; ZFPM1 (FOG1) reaches FOXN1 - the master regulator of thymic epithelial cell specification - alongside cytokine genes IL5, IFNG and FCER1G and hematopoietic TFs GATA2/NFE2; HHEX is a hematopoietic-progenitor homeobox factor with its own role in early thymic/parathyroid organogenesis. Together the four cover: specify lymphoid progenitors and thymic epithelium (HHEX, ZFPM1-FOXN1), commit B cells (EBF1), and license antigen-driven B/T interaction (AKNA-CD40/CD40L).
role_in_a: In COPD, chronic smoke-driven airway injury is known to induce ectopic peribronchial lymphoid structures (inducible bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue) with organized B-cell follicles and germinal centers. This module would supply the transcriptional machinery for that neogenesis: EBF1-driven B-lineage commitment feeding the follicle, AKNA/CD40-CD40L licensing germinal-center activation, and HHEX/ZFPM1 supporting the underlying hematopoietic and cytokine (IL5/IFNG) output.
role_in_b: In thymoma, the tumor arises from thymic epithelium and is well known clinically to disturb normal thymopoiesis; ZFPM1's direct reach to FOXN1 ties it to thymic epithelial identity itself. Thymoma is also classically associated with disordered lymphocyte output - Good syndrome (thymoma with hypogammaglobulinemia) reflects a defect on the B-lymphopoiesis axis EBF1 sits at, and paraneoplastic autoimmunity reflects abnormal T-B costimulatory signaling of the kind AKNA/CD40-CD40L governs.
shared_axis: Lung and thymus are both organs where the diseased state (chronically injured airway epithelium in COPD, neoplastic epithelium in thymoma) can host locally organized, ectopic-or-dysregulated lymphoid tissue built from the same B-lymphopoiesis-plus-costimulation transcriptional kit, which is why the same small factor set recurs across independent patient subgroups of both diseases.
reasoning: The module is nameable and mechanistically specific (FOXN1 via ZFPM1, CD40/CD40L via AKNA, B-lineage program via EBF1), and each disease is independently known to involve lymphoid-tissue biology on this axis (iBALT in COPD, Good syndrome/thymic lymphopoiesis defects in thymoma), so the pairing is not anatomically arbitrary. But the retrieved record does not itself document either connection: the only two placements available (EBF1, HHEX) are indirect - a longevity GWAS mentioning pulmonary disease and a lung-fibroblast miRNA study - and AKNA and ZFPM1 have no disease-specific literature at all, so the account rests on general biology rather than what was retrieved.
support: PMID 30642433 - places EBF1 in COPD only via a longevity/lifespan GWAS that mentions pulmonary disease, not lymphoid follicle biology specifically; PMID 28910321 - places HHEX in COPD via TGF-beta-regulated microRNAs in lung fibroblasts, not an immune/lymphoid context. No PMIDs above place AKNA or ZFPM1 in either disease.
how_to_falsify: In COPD lung tissue, compare single-cell/spatial expression of EBF1, AKNA and ZFPM1 between tertiary lymphoid follicles (iBALT) and non-follicular airway regions; the account predicts enrichment in follicles. In thymoma cohorts, test whether ZFPM1/FOXN1 co-expression in tumor epithelium and reduced EBF1-driven B-lineage output track with Good-syndrome (hypogammaglobulinemic) cases versus thymoma patients without it. If the factor signature is uniform across follicular and non-follicular tissue, or does not distinguish Good-syndrome from non-Good-syndrome thymoma, the account is falsified.
caveats: Support across the module is modest in absolute terms - the best factor (EBF1) holds in only 61/130 (47%) of patient-group comparisons, and the others are lower (58, 58, 49/130), so this is a recurrent-but-partial signal, not a near-universal one, and the 130 comparisons derive from only 2 independent cohort pairs, limiting true replication. The excluded single-view factors (OTP, HOXD10, IRX2, BPTF, TBX21, MXD4) do not overlap with this programme, so the account is not built on a subgroup-specific artifact. No tissue-generic exclusion list was supplied for this pair. Lung and thymus are anatomically distinct tissues, and the shared-axis claim (ectopic/dysregulated lymphoid organization) is a reasoning bridge, not a documented fact about this specific disease pair.
